# Productize the operator-based Feast deployment (Branch A)

## Description

Productize the operator-based Feast deployment topology: package Feast for
deployment through its operator in a form RHOAI supports — deployment
manifests, container image productization, and the integration surface the
Platform Operator enablement will build against. This branch epic applies only
if the deployment topology investigation selects the operator-based topology;
if the standalone per-project topology is selected instead, this epic is
dropped and the standalone branch applies.

## Scope

- Implement the operator-based deployment productization in the midstream
  Feast repository: deployment manifests and configuration for the
  operator-based topology, per the selected topology decision.
- Produce the productized container images for the operator-based deployment
  through the Feature Store build pipeline, consuming the productized image
  digests as configuration references (filled in at build time).
- Validate the deployment works on OpenShift in the productized form,
  including integration with customer-managed offline stores (managed
  offline-store infrastructure remains out of scope).
- Define the interface the Platform Operator enablement will integrate
  against (the operator's CRs and lifecycle surface) for the enablement work
  that builds on this deployment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The operator-based Feast deployment installs and runs on OpenShift from the
  productized manifests and images.
- The build pipeline is green for all images this deployment consumes, with
  productized digests referenced in the shipped configuration.
- The deployment works against a customer-provided offline store.
- The integration surface for Platform Operator enablement is documented and
  stable for the enablement work that follows.
- Deployment failure modes are documented (or link to upstream documentation)
  to the level needed for support.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): "Administrators can enable a supported Feature Store (Feast)
  ... with productized images" — this epic produces the productized,
  operator-based deployment that enablement turns on.

## Dependencies and Constraints

- Requires the midstream Feast repository and cleared licenses before the
  deployment contents are final.
- Applies only if the topology investigation selects the operator-based
  topology; otherwise this epic is removed.

# Platform Operator enablement for Feature Store, operator topology (Branch A)

## Description

Enable the Feature Store (Feast) through the Platform Operator like any other
managed RHOAI component, for the operator-based deployment topology:
administrators toggle the component on and the platform deploys and manages
it. This branch epic applies only if the topology investigation selects the
operator-based topology; it consumes the integration surface (operator CRs
and lifecycle) produced by the operator-based deployment productization.

## Scope

- Add Feature Store to the Platform Operator's managed component set using
  the operator-based deployment's CR and lifecycle surface, following the
  pattern used by other managed components.
- Administrator enablement: the component can be enabled/disabled through the
  Platform Operator, with the deployment lifecycle (install, upgrade, removal)
  managed accordingly.
- Reference the productized image digests for the operator-based deployment
  as configuration (digests available as an acceptance gate, not a build-time
  blocking dependency).
- Handle disablement cleanly: turning the component off removes the managed
  deployment without damaging customer data in customer-managed offline
  stores.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can enable the Feature Store through the Platform Operator
  and the operator-based deployment is installed and becomes functional;
  disabling it removes the managed deployment.
- The enablement follows the Platform Operator's established pattern for
  managed components.
- Productized image digests for the operator-based deployment are available
  and referenced in the operator configuration at execution time.
- Upgrade of the component through the Platform Operator works for at least
  one version step.
- Customer data in customer-managed offline stores survives enable/disable
  cycles.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): "Administrators can enable a supported Feature Store (Feast)
  through the Platform Operator like any other managed component, with
  productized images."

## Dependencies and Constraints

- Requires the operator-based deployment productization (its CRs and
  lifecycle surface) to exist and be stable before the operator integration
  can build against it.
- Applies only if the topology investigation selects the operator-based
  topology; otherwise this epic is removed.

# Select and validate the Feast productization deployment topology

## Description

Resolve the strategy's open question before any deployment or enablement work
starts: which Feast deployment topology RHOAI productizes first — the
operator-based deployment or the standalone server per project. Upstream Feast
supports both, but their supportability, lifecycle integration, and per-project
isolation characteristics differ. This investigation produces a documented
decision with evidence, so that the deployment implementation and the Platform
Operator enablement work can be scoped to exactly one topology, and so the
Dashboard integration knows which resource and endpoint surface to read.

## Scope

- Analyze both upstream Feast deployment topologies (operator-based deployment;
  standalone server per project) against product requirements: lifecycle
  management through the Platform Operator, per-project isolation, support
  burden, upgrade path, and alignment with how other managed RHOAI components
  are deployed.
- Evaluate supportability of each topology in a productized context (failure
  modes, observability, security posture, compatibility with
  customer-managed offline stores, since managed offline-store infrastructure
  is out of scope).
- Recommend one topology to productize first, with a documented rationale and
  the consequences for downstream work (deployment manifests, Platform
  Operator enablement surface, Dashboard resource/endpoint surface).
- Identify any prerequisite or follow-up work the selected topology implies
  that is not already covered by the midstream repository, build pipeline, and
  license validation efforts.

Deliverable: a decision document recording the selected topology, the evidence,
and the consequences for the deployment, enablement, and Dashboard
integrations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The decision document enumerates both candidate topologies and evaluates
  each against lifecycle integration via the Platform Operator, per-project
  isolation, support burden, and upgrade path.
- One topology is recommended with a recorded rationale and sign-off from the
  owning teams (Feature Store and Platform Operator).
- The consequences for downstream work are documented: the deployment surface
  the Feature Store team must productize, the enablement surface the Platform
  Operator team must integrate, and the resource/endpoint surface the
  Dashboard integration must read.
- Any prerequisite or follow-up work implied by the selected topology is
  identified and either confirmed as covered by existing work in this
  strategy or flagged for the strategy owner.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the chosen topology determines how the supported Feature Store
  is deployed and enabled through the Platform Operator.
- HLR-3 (P1): the chosen topology determines the endpoint/resource surface the
  Dashboard integration presents per project.

## Open Questions (resolved by this epic)

This epic is the resolution of the strategy's open question 1: "Which Feast
deployment topology do we productize first — the operator-based deployment or
the standalone server per project?"

# License validation for Feast and transitive dependencies

## Description

Run license scanning and validation over upstream Feast and its full
transitive dependency tree to confirm the Feature Store component can ship as
a supported, productized RHOAI component and that the Feast SDK can be
preinstalled in a supported workbench image. Feast is new to the platform, so
its dependency licenses have never been cleared.

## Scope

- Configure and run license scanning over the upstream Feast source tree and
  the container images planned for productization.
- Resolve the complete transitive dependency tree (including Python
  dependencies of the Feast SDK destined for workbench images) and check every
  dependency license against Red Hat's supported-license policy.
- Produce a license clearance report listing all dependencies, their licenses,
  and the disposition (approved, needs-review, blocked).
- For any needs-review or blocked dependency, document the finding and the
  mitigation options (version bump, exclusion, upstream change, or redesign of
  the productization approach).

Out of scope: choosing the deployment topology and any deployment code — this
epic validates the software being shipped, not how it is deployed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A license scan report exists covering upstream Feast and its transitive
  dependencies for both the container image and the workbench SDK surface.
- Every dependency has an explicit disposition; no unresolved findings remain,
  or each open finding has a documented owner and mitigation plan accepted by
  the owning teams.
- The clearance decision is recorded: Feast's dependency tree is shippable, or
  the specific blockers and required approach changes are documented for the
  downstream productization and workbench image work.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): productized, supported images require a cleared license profile.
- HLR-2 (P1): preinstalling the Feast SDK in a supported workbench image
  requires its transitive licenses to be cleared.

# Feast SDK preinstalled in a supported workbench image

## Description

Make the feature store reachable from data science workbenches: preinstall the
Feast SDK in at least one supported RHOAI workbench image, so data scientists
can connect to the feature store from a notebook without manual pip installs.
This covers the workbench-image side of workbench reachability; the feature
store itself is deployed and enabled through separate efforts.

## Scope

- Select the supported workbench image (or images) that will carry the Feast
  SDK preinstalled, following existing workbench image conventions.
- Add the Feast SDK and its required dependencies to the selected image
  build, at a version compatible with the productized Feature Store release
  baseline.
- Verify the SDK installs cleanly in the image build (dependency resolution,
  no conflicts with the image's existing package set) and that import works
  in a running workbench.
- Document the SDK version carried in each affected image.

Out of scope: Feast server/operator deployment and Platform Operator
enablement, and any feature-authoring UI (Dashboard presence is a separate
effort).

## Acceptance Criteria

- At least one supported workbench image ships with the Feast SDK
  preinstalled; the image and SDK version are documented.
- The SDK imports successfully and basic client operations can be initiated
  from a running workbench of that image against a feature store endpoint.
- The SDK version is compatible with the productized Feast release baseline
  selected for the midstream repository.
- The package addition does not regress the existing workbench image test
  suite.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): "Data scientists can reach the feature store from workbenches
  with the Feast SDK preinstalled in at least one supported workbench image."

## Dependencies and Constraints

- License clearance for the Feast SDK and its transitive dependencies must
  complete before the image contents are finalized; if licenses fail, the
  dependency set changes and this epic's scope is rewritten.

Show the Feature Store as an enabled component in the RHOAI Dashboard and link
users to its endpoints per project. This is a link-out integration only — the
out-of-scope statement excludes a feature-authoring UI in the Dashboard for
this release. Per the Dashboard architecture context

CRs and per-component feature flags/defaults through the OdhDashboardConfig

## Scope

- Add Dashboard presence for the Feature Store component: it appears as an
  enabled component when the platform has it enabled, following the
  per-component feature-flag/defaults pattern in the OdhDashboardConfig CR.
- Surface per-project links to the Feature Store endpoints for projects where
  the component is enabled (link-out only; no feature-authoring UI).
- Read the component's resource/endpoint surface from the Kubernetes API
  consistent with the deployment topology selected for productization (the
  Dashboard reads CRs; it owns no data plane).
- Cover the integration with the Dashboard's existing test conventions.

Out of scope: feature-authoring UI in the Dashboard, and any feature store
deployment or enablement logic — the Dashboard reads what the platform
deploys.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the Feature Store is enabled on the platform, the Dashboard shows it as
  an enabled component; when disabled, it is not shown.
- For each project where the component is enabled, the Dashboard links users
  to that project's Feature Store endpoints.
- The integration follows the OdhDashboardConfig feature-flag/defaults pattern
  used by other components, per the Dashboard architecture context.
- Dashboard test suite covers the new presence and link behavior.

  and links users to its endpoints per project."

## Dependencies and Constraints

- The deployment topology decision (operator-based vs. standalone server per
  project) must be resolved first: it determines the CR/endpoint surface this
  integration reads. The integration approach is rewritten if the topology
  decision changes it.

no build pipeline, and no operator integration — it is a **new component** (no
architecture context file exists for it), so the full onboarding chain is generated
